propositions: The test kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to per-test timeout (300s) firing via os._exit(1) from pytest-timeout's thread method, producing worker crash with no traceback.
The test's cost is unbounded: it processes 884 renderable units with ~1768 serial pandoc spawns in a single monolithic loop, measuring 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation (1.7x over budget).
Fixed by chunk-parametrizing the test with constant chunk size _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40, splitting 884 units into ~23 cases, each bounded to ~4.2s idle with 13x headroom.
All 884 corpus units remain byte-identity compared against the oracle (_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE stays 1, real pandoc on both sides); chunking adds no test parallelization barrier.
A coverage guard test ensures all chunks concatenate to exactly _renderable_units() with total >= 100, preventing silent unit drops.
The fix reduces worst-case from 504.8s to 38.05s (7.9x improvement) and closes the worker crash failure mode by construction, not by timeout tuning.
